persona: Residential listing agent (solo or small team)
title: I want to write a listing description for my new listing without staring at a blank page
workflowSummary: Gather the property basics first: address, beds, baths, square footage, three to five standout features, and the tone you want. Paste them into a free generator like SimpleListings and you get three drafts back in seconds with no account. Use ChatGPT or Claude instead if you want tighter control over the voice. Pick the draft that sounds most like you, then edit it properly: correct anything the AI guessed at, cut any wording that could read as a fair-housing problem, and add one specific detail only someone who walked the house would know. Paste the finished version into the MLS.
samplePrompt:
Write three versions of an MLS listing description for this property, each under 150 words.
Property: [beds/baths, square footage, property type, year built, city].
Standout features: [list 3-5].
Tone: [e.g. warm and straightforward, not luxury].
Rules: describe the property only, never the type of person who should live here. Do not mention families, schools, religion, or nationality. Do not invent any feature I have not listed.
beginnerNote: the free versions need no account and take one form fill. The editing pass is the only skill involved.
pricingNote: SimpleListings generator: free, no sign-up. ListingAI: tiers not published on the site. ChatGPT Plus approx. $20/mo. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Output is yours to publish. The listing agent remains responsible for fair-housing compliance and for factual accuracy - MLS rules put wrong bed/bath/sqft on you, not the tool.

persona: Listing agent marketing a vacant property
title: I want to make my empty listing photos look furnished without renting furniture
workflowSummary: Take a well-lit, straight-on photo of each empty room. Upload it, pick the room type and a furniture style that matches the buyer you actually expect, and the tool returns a furnished version in roughly ten seconds. Regenerate until the furniture sits sensibly on the floor and nothing floats or blocks a doorway - this is where AI staging most often fails. Download the unwatermarked file, then label it. Nearly every MLS in North America requires staged photos to carry a 'Virtually Staged' label on the image itself plus a note in the listing remarks.
samplePrompt:
Tool settings brief:
Style: [transitional / modern / traditional], neutral palette, mid-priced furniture.
Room: [living room].
Keep the existing flooring and wall colour. Do not add or remove windows, doors, or walls. Do not change the room's proportions.

MLS remarks line to copy:
"Some photos are virtually staged. Furniture and decor have been added digitally; images are marked 'Virtually Staged'."
beginnerNote: upload, pick a style, download. No design experience needed.
pricingNote: Virtual Staging AI: approx. $16/mo for 6 photos and approx. $19/mo for 20 photos on yearly billing. StageHQ: credit packs from approx. $19 for 20 photos, 3 free watermarked previews. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Paid credits generally include a commercial licence covering MLS, marketing and print. Structural changes - moving walls, adding rooms, altering the footprint - are prohibited by most state real estate commissions; furniture and decor only. MLS labelling is mandatory in most of North America and a small number require the unstaged 'before' photo alongside. Check your local MLS rules.

Edited images come back in minutes. Batch settings brief:
Batch: [address] full shoot.
Apply: colour correction, window pull on all interiors, perspective correction, lens correction.
Sky replacement: front and rear exterior shots only. Clear blue with light cloud, matched to the time of day the photos were taken.
Do not apply HDR to twilight shots.
Output: 4K JPEG, no watermark.
beginnerNote: drag and drop, no editing knowledge required.

If it does justify it, either hire a local service partner for a one-off scan, which is simplest, or subscribe and scan yourself with a compatible phone or 360 camera. Either way, understand the cost structure before you commit: tours stay live only while you keep paying hosting, and add-ons like schematic floor plans are billed on top.

Property: [address], [square footage], [property type].
I need: a 3D walkthrough tour hosted for at least [6] months, an unbranded link for the MLS, a branded link for my own marketing, and a schematic floor plan.

Paid tiers reported from approx. $10-12/mo (Starter) to approx. $69/mo (Professional) to $309+/mo (Business), plus approx. $20/mo hosting per active space. Hired scans commonly $200-$600 per listing. Figures vary widely across sources - VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING and do not quote a single number to a customer.

title: I want someone to answer my phone when I'm in a showing so I don't lose the lead
workflowSummary: Sign up and write the script: what your business is, what you want the AI to ask (budget, timeline, pre-approval, area), and what it must never say. Connect your calendar so it can book showings directly, and set transfer rules so a current client or an urgent-sounding call rings you immediately. Then forward your line to it only during showing hours and after hours, not all day, until you have listened to a full week of recordings and are satisfied with how it sounds. The failure mode is not the AI missing a call - it is the AI confidently saying something wrong about a listing.
samplePrompt:
Setup script to paste into the tool:
You are the front desk for [Name], a residential real estate agent in [area]. Greet callers warmly and briefly.
Ask: are they calling about a specific property, buying, or selling; what area; what timeline; and if buying, are they pre-approved.
Offer to book a showing on my calendar.
Never quote or negotiate a price, never give legal or lending advice, never confirm that an offer has been accepted.
If the caller says they are an existing client, or the call sounds urgent, transfer to me immediately.
End by confirming the caller's name, number, and best time to reach them.
beginnerNote: to set up. Somewhat to get right - the script needs two or three rounds of tuning before it sounds like your business rather than a generic call centre.
pricingNote: Reported entry plans from approx. $25-$50/mo for solo agents (Marlie from approx. $49/mo plus approx. $0.35/min; Nextiva XBert quoted at a flat $99/mo). Team plans $150-$400/mo. Many young vendors in this category - VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Call recording consent laws vary by jurisdiction - two-party-consent states require disclosure. A growing number of jurisdictions also require telling the caller they are speaking to an AI. Confirm both before switching it on, and check where call recordings are stored.

persona: Agent or small team buying portal leads (Zillow, Realtor.com, Facebook)
title: I want my new online leads texted back within a minute even when I'm asleep

tools.name: Follow Up Boss with Mod AI

workflowSummary: Connect the tool to wherever your leads already land, which is usually your CRM. Choose carefully which sources get enrolled: portal leads yes, referrals from your sphere no - a warm referral should never meet a bot first. The AI texts within seconds, holds a back-and-forth about timeline, budget, area and pre-approval, keeps following up for months if the lead goes quiet, and hands over to you when they are ready. Read the first week of transcripts yourself and take over any conversation where the lead is clearly asking for a human.
samplePrompt:
Assistant persona brief to configure:
You are the assistant for [Name] at [brokerage] in [market]. Your only job is to start a conversation and establish four things: buying or selling, what area, what timeline, and if buying, whether they are pre-approved.
Keep messages under two sentences and sound like a person texting, not a brochure.
Never quote a commission, never give a home value, never promise a price.
If they ask for a human, ask for a good time and hand off immediately.
If they do not reply, follow up on a slowing schedule. Stop entirely if they ask you to.
beginnerNote: the tool itself is easy to run, but it needs a CRM already in place and the contracts are annual, so it is not a casual try-it-and-see purchase.
pricingNote: Not published. The vendor's pricing page is quote-only and states annual contracts with a 20% premium for month-to-month. Third parties report $299-$499/mo plus a reported one-time onboarding fee around $2,000. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Highest legal-risk workflow in this batch. Automated SMS is regulated - US TCPA requires prior express written consent for marketing texts and an honoured opt-out, and the agent, not the vendor, is normally the one fined. Vendor-published conversion statistics are self-reported and independently unverified; treat them as marketing.

persona: Listing-focused agent farming a specific neighbourhood
title: I want to know which homeowners in my farm are most likely to sell this year
workflowSummary: Choose a territory you can genuinely service and afford to market to for a full year, because these are annual commitments and the value only appears across repeated touches. The platform scores homeowners on ownership length, equity, demographics and online behaviour, then hands you a ranked list plus automated mail and ad campaigns. Work the top of the list personally - call, door-knock, handwritten note - and let the automated campaigns cover the long tail. The data is a targeting aid, not a substitute for the farming routine itself.
samplePrompt:
Vetting questions to ask before signing (not an AI prompt):
1. Is my territory exclusive, or are you selling the same list to other agents in my area?
2. What is the total 12-month cost including direct mail and ads?
3. What accuracy rate do you publish, and measured against what?
4. Can I cancel mid-term, and what is the penalty?
5. Can I see a 90-day sample of last year's predictions for my ZIP so I can check them against actual sales?
6. If I cancel, can I export the contacts I have worked?
beginnerNote: high cost, long contract, and the data is only worth anything if you already have a consistent farming routine to plug it into. Not a first AI purchase.
pricingNote: Not published. Third-party reports diverge sharply: one cites a $99/mo platform fee plus approx. $1.25-$1.50 per property per month for campaigns; others report $300-$600/mo territory pricing on 12-month contracts. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING - this spread is too wide to quote to a customer.
accessNotes: Lead data is licensed, not owned - check export rights on cancellation. Exclusivity is often not guaranteed. Direct mail and calling remain subject to do-not-call and mail regulations. Third-party reviews of this category are mixed on both accuracy and contract terms; sanity-check before recommending.

persona: Agent preparing for a listing appointment
title: I want to put together a pricing report for a seller without spending three hours on it

tools.name: ChatGPT or Claude for the narrative only

workflowSummary: Start in the MLS or RPR, because that is where the defensible comp data lives. Pull sold, pending and active comps, adjust for beds, baths, square footage and condition, and settle on your own price opinion before any AI is involved. Then use Cloud CMA to turn that into the branded, presentable report, and optionally use a general AI assistant to draft the narrative section that explains your reasoning to the seller in plain language. The division of labour matters: the AI writes the story, you set the number.
samplePrompt:
Here are the comps I selected and the adjustments I made: [paste].
My recommended list price is [$X].
Write a one-page explanation for the seller in plain language covering: why I chose these comps, what the adjustments mean, what the days-on-market data suggests about pricing strategy, and what is likely to happen if we price above my recommendation.
Do not change my price. Do not change my comp selection. Do not add any statistic I have not given you.
beginnerNote: for the report and the narrative. The comp selection and the price itself are judgement work and should not be delegated to a tool.
pricingNote: RPR is included with NAR membership at no additional cost. Cloud CMA is frequently paid for by the local MLS as a member benefit - check before buying a seat. Published figures conflict: Capterra lists from $49 per feature per month; other sources report approx. $25-$60 per agent per month. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: A CMA is the agent's professional opinion of value and is not an appraisal - it must never be presented as one. Do not let an AI-generated valuation stand in as the price opinion; the agent is accountable for the number. Score of 5 applies to Cloud CMA and RPR as products, not to AI-generated valuations, which should be treated as a 2.

persona: Agent or transaction coordinator managing a live deal
title: I want the key dates and deadlines pulled out of a signed purchase agreement automatically

tools.name: ChatGPT or Claude for a plain-language client summary

workflowSummary: Upload the executed purchase agreement plus every counter and addendum. The tool reads it and pulls out the parties, price, earnest money, and each contingency with its deadline, then builds a task list and calendar from those dates - typically in under a minute, including from handwritten fields. Then verify every extracted date against the contract yourself before you rely on any of it. Use the plain-language summary separately, to walk your client through what they actually signed.
samplePrompt:
For a general assistant, when you are not using a dedicated tool:
I have attached an executed residential purchase agreement. Produce:
1. A table of every deadline, with the exact contract language it comes from and the page it appears on.
2. A plain-language summary for my client of what they agreed to, at roughly a 9th-grade reading level.
3. A list of anything unusual or missing compared with a standard [state] residential contract.
Quote the contract language for every date. Where a date depends on a calculation such as '7 business days after acceptance', show the calculation and flag it for me to verify. Do not give legal advice.
beginnerNote: for the dedicated tools - upload and read. Somewhat with a general assistant, because you have to know what to ask for.
pricingNote: Not published on either vendor's feature page. DocJacket advertises a free trial. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Not legal advice, and no vendor claims otherwise. Uploading an executed contract means sending clients' names, addresses and financial terms to a third party - check the vendor's retention policy and whether your brokerage permits it. Vendor claims of 'human-level accuracy' are unverified. A missed contingency deadline is a career-level error, so this is assist-only: every date needs human verification.

persona: New agent, or any agent whose headshot is out of date
title: I want a professional headshot for my listings and business cards without booking a photographer
workflowSummary: Take six to fifteen clear, well-lit selfies from different angles, with a few different expressions and outfits, and no sunglasses, hats or other people in frame. Upload them, choose backdrop and attire styles that match how you actually dress for work, and wait somewhere between twenty minutes and two hours. You will get back dozens to a hundred images, most unusable and a handful genuinely good. Pick one that looks like you: a headshot that flatters you into someone else is worse than no headshot at all, because clients meet you in person.
samplePrompt:
Style brief for the generator:
Attire: business casual - open-collar shirt or blazer, no tie.
Backdrop: neutral studio grey, plus a soft office or outdoor blur.
Expression: warm and approachable, natural smile.
Keep my actual hair length, glasses, and skin tone unchanged. No heavy retouching - leave visible skin texture and my natural age.
beginnerNote: the whole process is upload, choose, wait. Output quality depends almost entirely on the quality of the selfies you feed it.
pricingNote: One-time packages reported roughly $19-$75 (HeadshotPro $29-$59; Aragon approx. $35 for 40 images up to approx. $75 for 100). Team and bulk discounts common. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Your face is biometric data. Check the vendor's policy: some delete input photos after 30 days and exclude training use, others do not. A small number of brokerages and MLSs have rules on AI-generated agent photos - check yours before it goes on a yard sign.

persona: Agent who knows they should post on social media but never does
title: I want a month of social media posts for my real estate business without making them from scratch
workflowSummary: Subscribe to a real-estate-specific content library, download the month's calendar, and swap in your branding, your photos and one local fact per post. Note that most of these libraries hand you templates and captions but do not publish for you, so you will still need a scheduling tool on top. Rewrite at least a third of every caption in your own words. The whole point is that people can tell it is you - and every other agent in your market may be subscribing to exactly the same library.
samplePrompt:
Here is a template caption from a real estate content library: [paste].
Rewrite it in my voice: [describe yourself - e.g. dry and practical, no exclamation marks, no emojis, 12-year agent in [area] who mostly works with first-time buyers].
Keep the same core message and call to action. Make it sound like something I would actually text a friend. Under 80 words.
beginnerNote: download, edit, post. The judgement call is how much to rewrite, not how to use the tool.
pricingNote: Reported figures conflict across sources for the same product: approx. $54/mo, $74/mo, and $108/mo for teams all appear for Coffee & Contracts. Agent Crate reported at approx. $29/mo; RealEstateContent.ai at approx. $99/mo. Yearly plans typically discount. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING - do not quote a single figure.
sourceType: Vendor site (blog page - no public pricing page located)
accessNotes: Template licences normally cover your own marketing but not resale or sharing with other agents. Check whether the licence survives cancellation - several do not, which can mean taking published posts down. The real risk here is sameness, not legality: several agents in one market running identical graphics.

persona: Agent staying in touch with past clients and sphere of influence
title: I want to send my past clients a monthly market update without writing it every month
intentLabels: stay in touch with past clients
workflowSummary: Two routes. The subscription route: a tool like MarketMailer pulls market data and curated local news and drafts the newsletter around your name and market, and you review and send. The DIY route costs nothing beyond what you already pay for and takes about twenty minutes: gather your own MLS stats plus two or three local news items and an upcoming event, run the prompt below, and paste the result into whatever you already send email from. Either way the numbers must come from your MLS, cited by name and month - not from the AI's own knowledge.
samplePrompt:
Write my monthly newsletter for past clients and my sphere in [area]. Use only the information below - do not add any statistic, price, or news item I have not given you.
Market stats from [MLS name], [month]: [paste].
Local news and events: [paste].
My recent activity: [paste].
Format: short intro in my voice; a 'what the numbers actually mean' section in plain language; the local roundup; a soft close inviting people to reply with questions.
Under 500 words. No hype, and do not write 'now is a great time to buy'.
beginnerNote: the DIY route needs no new tool at all, just twenty minutes and a copy-paste.
pricingNote: MarketMailer: pricing not published on its agent page. AgentReach: reported from $49/mo. DIY route: costs only your existing email tool plus an AI subscription (approx. $20/mo, or a free tier). VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Bulk email is regulated - CAN-SPAM in the US, GDPR and PECR in the EU and UK, DPDP in India. You need a working unsubscribe link, a physical postal address, and a lawful basis for the list. Past clients are not automatically an opted-in marketing list. Trust score of 4 covers the workflow; any market statistic the AI produces unprompted should be treated as a 2 and replaced with MLS data.

persona: Agent trying to get found on Google and in AI search results
title: I want to write a neighbourhood guide for my website that people actually find
intentLabels: how to rank as a realtor on Google
workflowSummary: Pick one neighbourhood you genuinely know, because a page about an area you have never sold in will neither rank nor convert. Gather the raw material yourself: current median price and days on market from your MLS, transport and amenity facts, and three or four things only a local would say. Let the AI structure and draft it, then add what it cannot know - which streets are quiet, where the traffic backs up, what the HOA is actually like in practice. Publish it as a permanent page rather than a dated blog post, and link your listings in that area to it.
samplePrompt:
Write a neighbourhood guide page for [neighbourhood, city] for my real estate website, aimed at buyers considering the area.
Use only these facts: [paste MLS stats with month and source, transport, amenities, price ranges].
Structure it with question-style headings a buyer would actually type.
Include a short 'who this area suits and who it doesn't' section that is honest about the downsides.
800-1,000 words, plain language, no marketing superlatives.
Do not invent statistics, school ratings, crime data, or demographics.
Leave a clearly marked [LOCAL INSIGHT] placeholder in three places where I should add something only a local agent would know.
beginnerNote: to produce a draft. Somewhat to get results, since ranking takes months of consistent publishing rather than one good page.
pricingNote: Free on any AI assistant's free tier; approx. $20/mo for a paid assistant. Managed platforms are quote-only and considerably more expensive. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Significant fair-housing exposure. In the US it is unlawful to describe an area by the race, religion, national origin, family status or disability of its residents, and AI drafts drift toward exactly that - 'family-friendly', 'great for young professionals'. Describe the property and the place, never the people. Do not publish school ratings or crime data as a selling point. Have a compliance-aware human read every page before it goes live.

persona: Independent landlord or small investor with 1-20 units
title: I want to screen a tenant and get a compliant lease without hiring a property manager
workflowSummary: List the unit and collect applications through the platform so you never handle the applicant's identity or bank details yourself - the screening report comes to you and the applicant pays the fee. Generate a state-specific lease from the template, then run the AI lease audit, which checks the document against your state's landlord-tenant law and flags things like non-compliant deposit or disclosure clauses. Treat that audit as a pre-lawyer screen, not as legal advice. E-sign, then run rent and maintenance through the tenant portal so everything is logged in one place.
samplePrompt:
For a general AI second opinion on the lease:
I am a small landlord in [state or country]. Here is my draft lease: [paste].
List anything that looks non-standard or potentially non-compliant with local landlord-tenant law. Quote the specific clause and explain why it is a concern. Rank by risk.
Do not rewrite the lease. Tell me plainly which items I should take to a lawyer rather than fix myself.
You are not my lawyer and this is not legal advice.
beginnerNote: the free tier genuinely covers listing, screening and the AI tools, so it can be tested with no spend.
pricingNote: Free plan at $0 to the landlord. Paid tiers reported at $149/yr (Essentials) and $199/yr (Pro), annual billing only. Tenant-side fees apply on every plan: screening reported at approx. $55 on free and $45 on paid, ACH approx. $2 per payment on free, card approx. 3.49%; a state-specific lease reported at approx. $59 a la carte on the free plan. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING - 'free' is free to the landlord, not to the tenancy.
accessNotes: US tenant screening is governed by the FCRA - an adverse action notice is required if you decline based on a report. Fair-housing rules apply to how you advertise and how you screen. The AI lease audit is explicitly not legal advice per the vendor's own disclaimer.

persona: Property manager or landlord fielding after-hours maintenance calls
title: I want tenant maintenance requests handled at 2am without me picking up the phone
workflowSummary: Route tenant calls, texts and portal requests to the AI. It asks diagnostic questions, walks the tenant through the obvious fixes - tripped breaker, disposal reset, filter change - classifies the request as emergency or routine, and only dispatches a vendor or wakes a human when it needs to. Everything is logged as a work order. You set the escalation rules, and getting those right before you switch it on is the entire job: an AI that misclassifies a gas smell as routine is a habitability problem, not a software bug.
samplePrompt:
Escalation rules to configure:
Always escalate to a human immediately, with no troubleshooting: any smell of gas, smoke or fire; active water leak or flooding; sewage backup; no heat when the outdoor temperature is below [X]; no working lock on an exterior door; any report involving injury; and any tenant who asks twice to speak to a person.
Attempt guided troubleshooting first for: tripped breakers, garbage disposal jams, HVAC filter and thermostat issues, and appliance settings.
Never promise a repair time, never quote a cost, and never tell a tenant that a repair is not the landlord's responsibility.
beginnerNote: the tools themselves are straightforward, but you need a real vendor list and clear escalation rules in place first, and those are not something the software writes for you.
pricingNote: Varies by model. TenantCloud reported with a free core plan and premium from approx. $12.42/mo billed annually. Latchel and AppFolio are custom-quoted by unit count. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Habitability and emergency-response obligations sit with the landlord or manager, not the vendor - a misclassified emergency is your liability. Vendor-reported figures such as '30-50% of requests resolved without a vendor visit' come from self-reported industry case studies and are not independently verified. Check whether the vendor records calls and whether your jurisdiction requires disclosing that the tenant is speaking to an AI.

persona: Listing agent who wants every marketing piece for a new listing in one pass
title: I want to turn one new listing into all my marketing pieces at once

tools.name: Matterport Marketing Cloud (if you already have a 3D scan)

workflowSummary: Enter the listing once - address, details, photos - and the platform generates the pieces off that single record: MLS-ready description, a CMA, staged images, a listing video, social posts, a single-property website, and seller-facing performance updates. The value is not that each piece beats a specialist tool, because it usually does not. The value is that everything is consistent and you enter the data once. Review each output separately rather than trusting the bundle, since a bundled tool also means a bundled set of mistakes.
samplePrompt:
Listing brief for the campaign:
Property: [address], [beds/baths/sqft], [price].
Standout features: [3-5].
Target buyer: [e.g. first-time buyers, downsizers].
Tone: [warm and factual].
Rules for every generated piece: describe the property, never the type of buyer. No references to families, schools, religion or nationality. Do not state any figure I have not provided. Mark any virtually staged image as 'Virtually Staged'.
beginnerNote: one data entry, everything generated from it.
pricingNote: Not published on the vendor's homepage. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Confirm output ownership and whether the single-property website stays live after cancellation. MLS staging-disclosure rules apply to any staged image the platform produces, exactly as they would from a standalone staging tool. Newer entrant with limited independent review coverage - sanity-check before recommending to a customer.

persona: Buyer's agent, or a buyer doing early research
title: I want to search for homes by describing what I actually want instead of using filters

tools.name: John L. Scott AI Home Search
your brokerage's own AI search if it has one

workflowSummary: Instead of setting dropdown filters, type a full sentence describing what the buyer wants, including the soft criteria filters cannot capture - natural light, a quiet street, a workable home office. These tools read listing text and in some cases analyse listing photos, so they surface homes a filter search would miss. Treat the output as a shortlist to react to, not an answer: most of these systems only see what is in the MLS, so off-market and coming-soon inventory is invisible to them, and photo analysis is still the least reliable part.
samplePrompt:
I'm looking for a home in [area] under [$X]. Here's what actually matters to us, in priority order:
1. [e.g. a real home office with a door, not a nook]
2. [e.g. under a 30-minute drive to [workplace]]
3. [e.g. natural light - we hate dark rooms]
4. [e.g. a yard big enough for a dog]
Deal-breakers: [e.g. busy road, no garage, HOA over $400/month].
Show me matches and tell me for each one which of my criteria it does NOT meet.
beginnerNote: it is a search box. The skill is writing a description that includes the deal-breakers, not just the wish list.
pricingNote: Free to consumers on the major portals. Brokerage-side deployments reported at $200-$5,000/mo; investor subscriptions $50-$500/mo. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
sourceType: Directory / knowledge-base listing (weakest source in this batch - see README)
accessNotes: These tools index MLS data only - off-market inventory will not appear. Photo-based matching is imperfect and can surface homes that do not have the feature claimed. Never let a buyer rely on an AI summary of a listing in place of the listing itself or a showing.

persona: Buyer's agent preparing a client for a specific address
title: I want a neighbourhood report for an address so my buyer knows what living there is actually like
intentLabels: what's it like to live here

tools.name: your MLS's built-in neighbourhood tool if it licenses one

workflowSummary: Generate the report from the property address rather than the postcode, since two addresses in the same postcode can score very differently on transit, quiet and amenity access. Read it before you send it, and lead the conversation with the scores that match what the buyer told you mattered. Send it as supporting material after a showing rather than as a substitute for driving the area with them at the time of day they will actually be commuting.
samplePrompt:
Here is the neighbourhood report for [address]: [paste the scores and data].
My buyer's priorities, in their own words, were: [paste].
Write a short summary for them covering: which of their priorities this location genuinely delivers on, which it does not, and two or three things they should check in person before deciding.
Use only the data I have pasted. Do not add statistics, school ratings, crime figures, or any description of who lives in the area.
beginnerNote: to generate. The judgement is in which sections you surface and which you leave alone.
pricingNote: Not published - Local Logic sells to brokerages, MLSs and portals rather than individual agents, so many agents already have it free through their MLS. Check your MLS dashboard before buying anything. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: SERIOUS STEERING RISK. These reports include demographic data. In the US, directing a buyer toward or away from an area based on the race, religion, national origin, family status or disability of its residents is unlawful steering, and handing over a demographic breakdown unprompted can constitute it. Give buyers the tool and let them pull their own demographic data; keep your own commentary to the property and the physical location.

persona: Buyer or buyer's agent before writing an offer
title: I want to check the flood, wildfire and insurance risk on a house before we offer on it

tools.name: the risk panels already embedded on Zillow and Redfin listings
RPR (First Street is integrated for NAR members)

workflowSummary: Look up the specific address, not the neighbourhood - elevation and distance to water can put two homes on the same street in different risk bands. Read the five risk types (flood, wildfire, wind, heat, air quality) and the 30-year projection, not just today's score. Then take the practical step that actually matters: get an insurance quote on that address before the inspection contingency expires. A high risk score is not automatically a reason to walk, but an uninsurable or $9,000-a-year premium changes the affordability maths entirely.
samplePrompt:
Here is the climate risk report for [address]: [paste scores and projections].
Explain to my buyer, in plain language and under 300 words: what each score means in practice, which risks are worth acting on and which are background noise at this level, and exactly what questions they should ask an insurance broker about this specific property.
Do not tell them whether to buy the house. Do not estimate an insurance premium - say that they need a real quote.
beginnerNote: basic property lookups are free and require no account.
pricingNote: Basic property-level information is free (First Street is a non-profit; Risk Factor data is embedded free on Zillow, Redfin and RPR). Paid subscriptions add detail and report sharing. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: These are modelled projections, not guarantees, and they are not a substitute for a FEMA flood determination or a real insurance quote. Some states require specific hazard disclosures - a risk score does not satisfy a statutory disclosure obligation. Agents should share the tool rather than interpret the risk themselves; interpreting it edges toward advice you are not licensed to give.

persona: Buyer, or buyer's agent, the day the inspection report lands
title: I want this 40-page inspection report explained to me in plain English

tools.name: Claude or ChatGPT with the PDF (redact names first)

workflowSummary: Upload the report and ask for a summary organised by severity, not by the order the inspector walked the house - reports are structured by system, which buries the important items among the trivial ones. Get the plain-English version, the list of items worth asking the inspector about, and the list of things that are just normal for a house of that age. Then call the inspector. The AI can only read what is in the report; the inspector knows what was inaccessible, what was not tested, and what the photos do not show.
samplePrompt:
I've attached a home inspection report for a house I'm considering. Please give me:
1. The top five findings a buyer should actually care about, ranked by potential cost and safety, with the report's own wording quoted for each.
2. Which findings are normal wear for a [year]-built home rather than problems.
3. A list of specific follow-up questions I should ask the inspector, including anything the report marks as 'monitor', 'not inspected' or 'inaccessible'.
Do not tell me whether to buy the house or whether something is a deal-breaker - you do not know my market, my budget or my risk tolerance.
beginnerNote: upload and read. The one bit of discipline required is redacting personal details before uploading.
pricingNote: HomeReader and HomeInsight AI both advertise a free first report, then paid tiers not published on the landing page. General assistants: free tier or approx. $20/mo. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Inspection reports carry buyer and seller names and the property address on the cover page - redact before uploading to a general assistant, or use a private workspace. AI cannot assess what the inspector could not see and will not flag omissions from scope. Agents should be careful not to characterise findings as 'minor' or 'a deal-breaker' - that is close to giving an opinion on condition, which most licences do not cover.

persona: Buyer's agent drafting the repair request after inspection
title: I want to turn the inspection findings into a repair request I can actually send the seller
intentLabels: how much will this cost to fix

tools.name: a local contractor quote for anything material

workflowSummary: Decide with your buyer what they actually want first - a repair, a credit, or a price reduction - because the three read very differently to a seller. Use a tool to get indicative repair cost ranges so the ask is anchored to something, then draft the request. Keep it short and to the items that matter; a request listing twenty-two findings including a loose doorknob invites the seller to refuse the whole thing. For anything above a few thousand, get a real contractor quote rather than relying on an AI estimate.
samplePrompt:
Here are the inspection findings we want to raise: [paste the specific items and the report's wording].
My buyer wants to ask for: [a credit of $X / these specific repairs / a price reduction].
Draft a repair request to the listing agent that is professional, brief, and does not sound adversarial. For each item, state the finding factually and what we are asking for. Do not include estimated costs unless I have given them to you. Do not threaten to terminate.
Then give me a shorter fallback version covering only the [two] most serious items, in case the first is refused.
beginnerNote: drafting is easy, but deciding what to ask for and how hard to push is negotiation judgement the tool cannot supply.
pricingNote: HomeInsight AI advertises a free first report; paid plans not published. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING - AI repair cost estimates in particular should never be quoted to a client as a real number.
accessNotes: AI-generated repair cost estimates are not quotes and vary enormously by region and contractor availability. Do not present them to a buyer or a seller as costings. Repair requests are contract amendments in most states - check whether your jurisdiction requires a specific form rather than a letter.

persona: Buyer under contract on a condo or HOA property, and their agent
title: I want to know what's actually in the 300 pages of HOA documents before my review period expires
intentLabels: what am I agreeing to in this HOA

tools.name: Claude with the document set (for a general read)

workflowSummary: The review window is usually days, and the packet is usually hundreds of pages, which is why most buyers skim and sign. Upload the full set - CC&Rs, bylaws, rules, minutes - and get a structured report on the things that actually change a buyer's life: rental restrictions, pet limits, architectural approval requirements, what can and cannot be modified, and pending litigation. Prioritise tools that cite the page for every claim so you can verify the important findings yourself rather than trusting a summary. Send anything material to a lawyer within the review period, not after it.
samplePrompt:
I've attached the HOA governing documents for a property I'm buying. Produce a structured summary covering:
1. Rental and short-term-let restrictions - quote the exact clause and give the page number.
2. Pet restrictions, vehicle and parking rules, and anything restricting what I can do to the exterior or interior.
3. Architectural approval requirements and the process for getting approval.
4. Any mention of litigation, disputes, or enforcement actions.
5. Anything that reads as unusual for an HOA of this type.
Cite the page for every single item. If something is ambiguous, say so rather than resolving it. Flag which items I should take to a lawyer. This is not legal advice.
beginnerNote: for the dedicated tools. The hard part is getting the complete document set out of the seller or HOA in time.
pricingNote: GoverningDocs advertises a free first report and a free CC&R analysis tool. Paid tiers not published on the landing page. For comparison, the same page cites attorney review at $500-$2,000. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Not legal advice. General-purpose assistants are a poor fit for this specific task - the vendor cites published hallucination rates on niche material, and a fabricated or missed clause on a $600,000 purchase is not a recoverable error. Prefer tools that cite source pages, and verify every material finding against the document yourself before relying on it.

persona: Buyer purchasing in a condo, strata or townhome association
title: I want to know if this condo building is financially healthy or if I'll get hit with a special assessment

tools.name: a lender or accountant for anything borderline

workflowSummary: This is a different question from what the HOA rules say, and it is the one that costs buyers money after closing. Upload the reserve study, budget, financial statements and the last two years of meeting minutes together - the signal is usually in the gap between them, where minutes discuss deferred repairs the budget does not fund. Look for percent-funded status, deferred maintenance, recent or pending assessments, and insurance adequacy. Minutes are the most revealing document in the packet and the one buyers most often skip.
samplePrompt:
I've attached a condo association's reserve study, budget, financial statements and recent meeting minutes.
Tell me:
1. What is the reserve fund's percent-funded status, and what does that number mean in practice?
2. What major components (roof, elevators, plumbing, facade) are near the end of their stated useful life, and is there funded reserve for them?
3. Does anything in the meeting minutes discuss repairs, litigation or assessments that the budget does not appear to fund?
4. Have there been special assessments in the past three years?
Cite the document and page for every point. Where the documents contradict each other, say so rather than picking one.
beginnerNote: the analysis is automated, but interpreting reserve funding levels takes some context, and the tool is only as good as the documents you feed it.
pricingNote: Not published. The vendor states flexible pricing from individual pay-per-report options for homebuyers up to annual and enterprise subscriptions. Coverage stated as US and Canada. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Not financial or legal advice. An incomplete document packet produces a falsely reassuring report - if minutes or the reserve study are missing, that absence is itself the finding. Lenders have their own condo warrantability criteria which this will not tell you; check separately if financing is involved.

persona: Buyer-investor, or an agent working with one
title: I want to know if this rental property will actually cash flow before I make an offer
intentLabels: is this a good investment property

tools.name: your lender for real financing terms

workflowSummary: Import the property from public records or a listing, then correct the imported numbers - the estimated rent and taxes are the two that are most often wrong and they drive everything downstream. Enter your real financing terms rather than a placeholder rate, itemise closing costs, rehab and holding costs, and put in a vacancy and maintenance allowance rather than assuming twelve months of rent. Then run the same property at a worse rent and a higher rate. A deal that only works on the optimistic case is not a deal.
samplePrompt:
Here are the numbers from my analysis of [address]: [paste purchase price, rent estimate, taxes, insurance, HOA, financing terms, vacancy and maintenance assumptions, cash flow, cap rate, cash-on-cash].
Stress-test this for me:
1. Which of my assumptions is the deal most sensitive to?
2. What happens to cash flow if rent comes in 10% below estimate and vacancy runs at 8%?
3. What am I likely to have left out entirely? Assume I am a first-time investor.
Do not tell me whether to buy it. Do not invent numbers I have not given you.
beginnerNote: to run the numbers. No to interpreting them well on your first deal - the tool will happily produce a confident-looking return on bad inputs.
pricingNote: Free Starter plan reported as covering up to 15 properties. Paid tiers reported at approx. $10/mo (Plus) and $20/mo (Pro), billed annually with a 14-day trial. Vendor's own pricing page not directly captured. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Rent and value estimates are automated and frequently off in specific submarkets - verify against real comparable rentals before relying on them. An agent running these numbers for a client is close to giving investment advice; keep the analysis in the client's hands and let them own the assumptions.

persona: First-time buyer at the start of the process, and their agent
title: I want to work out how much house I can actually afford before I start looking
intentLabels: how much house can I afford

tools.name: a general AI assistant to explain the output

workflowSummary: Run the calculator honestly, including the debts buyers tend to leave out - car finance, student loans, minimum card payments. Then do the step the calculator does not: separate what you can borrow from what you want to spend. Lenders will approve to a ratio that leaves some households uncomfortable. Get a real pre-approval before touring, because a calculator output is not a lender commitment and in most markets you now need a written buyer agreement and a pre-approval before you see anything anyway.
samplePrompt:
Here's my situation: gross annual income [$X], monthly debts [$Y broken down], savings available for down payment and closing [$Z], estimated property tax and insurance for [area] [$A].
Explain in plain language:
1. What price range the standard lending ratios suggest, and how you got there.
2. What my monthly payment would actually look like at that price, itemised - principal, interest, taxes, insurance, PMI if applicable, HOA.
3. The difference between what a lender would approve and what would leave me comfortable, and what questions I should ask myself about that gap.
You are not a lender and this is not a pre-approval. Do not guess at an interest rate - tell me to get a current quote.
beginnerNote: free, no account, and the major calculators are well-designed.
pricingNote: Free. Fannie Mae's calculator is a public non-commercial tool; portal and lender calculators are free lead-generation tools. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING (that these remain free and publicly accessible).
accessNotes: A calculator result is not a pre-approval and must never be presented as one. Agents should be careful here: discussing what a buyer can afford shades into loan origination advice, which is separately licensed in most jurisdictions. Refer to a lender rather than interpreting the output for them.

persona: Buyer approaching closing, and their agent
title: I want to know how much cash I actually need on closing day, not just the down payment
intentLabels: what do I pay at closing

tools.name: your lender's Loan Estimate (the authoritative document)
a general AI assistant to explain the Loan Estimate line by line

workflowSummary: Start with an estimate to set expectations early, then switch to the real document as soon as you have it. The Loan Estimate the lender is required to provide is the authoritative figure and it is standardised, which makes it comparable across lenders. Use an AI assistant to walk the buyer through it line by line - most first-time buyers have never seen one and do not know which lines are shoppable and which are fixed. Reconcile the Closing Disclosure against the Loan Estimate before closing; unexplained increases are worth questioning.
samplePrompt:
I've attached my mortgage Loan Estimate. Explain it to me line by line as if I've never bought a house:
1. What each section is and what the charge is for.
2. Which of these costs I can shop around for and which are fixed by the lender or government.
3. What my total cash to close is and what it is made up of.
4. Anything on here that looks unusual or worth asking my lender about.
Do not tell me whether this is a good loan. Do not compare it to rates you think are current.
beginnerNote: the estimate is one form fill; understanding the Loan Estimate is where the value is.
pricingNote: Free. Portal calculators are free lead-generation tools; the Loan Estimate is provided free by the lender and is legally required in the US. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: A Loan Estimate contains the buyer's loan terms and personal financial details - redact or use a private workspace before uploading to a general assistant. Estimated closing costs are not binding; only the lender's disclosures are. Agents should not interpret loan terms for a client beyond explaining vocabulary.

persona: Buyer's agent running a multi-property showing day
title: I want to plan a showing day for my buyers that doesn't waste half of it driving

tools.name: whatever showing system your MLS provides

workflowSummary: Build the full list of stops before you start requesting appointments - scheduling as you add addresses means redoing the schedule every time you add one. Let the route optimiser sort the stops by drive time, then request all the appointments in one batch. Keep it to four to six homes; beyond about seven, buyers get decision fatigue and the houses blur together, which is worse than seeing fewer. Send the buyer the tour itinerary in advance with the addresses and times so they can look them up beforehand.
samplePrompt:
Here are the homes on tomorrow's tour, in the order the routing tool put them: [paste addresses, times, prices, key details].
Write a short itinerary email to my buyers covering: the schedule, the address and headline detail for each stop, and one specific thing to look at or think about at each one based on what they told me matters ([paste their priorities]).
End with a note asking them to jot down a one-line reaction after each house.
Keep it under 300 words. Do not describe the neighbourhoods or who lives in them.
beginnerNote: the routing is one click once the stops are in.
pricingNote: ShowingSmart states it is included as a benefit for all MLS subscribers in participating MLSs, so many agents already have this free. ShowingTime is similarly often MLS-provided. Check your MLS before paying for anything. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Availability depends entirely on which showing system your MLS has contracted - these are not tools an individual agent generally buys standalone. ShowingCart route planning was desktop-only at the time of the vendor's documentation; check current mobile support.

persona: Buyer's agent showing several homes in a day
title: I want to remember what each buyer said about each house without taking notes during the showing
intentLabels: what did they say about house three

tools.name: Rechat AI Memo (if you are on Rechat)

workflowSummary: Get consent first and out loud - this is the whole ballgame on this workflow. Then let the recorder run during the walkthrough, or dictate a voice memo in the car immediately after each house while it is fresh. The tool transcribes and pulls out what the buyer liked, what they objected to, and any follow-up you promised. Review the summary the same evening and move the real decisions into your CRM. The value shows up two weeks later when a similar listing appears and you know exactly why they passed on the last one.
samplePrompt:
Here's the transcript from today's showings with [buyer names]: [paste].
Produce:
1. A short profile of what they actually want, based on what they said rather than what they told me at the buyer consultation - flag anywhere the two differ.
2. Per property: what they liked, what they objected to, and how strong the objection sounded.
3. Every commitment I made, with what I promised and by when.
4. Three questions I should ask them before the next tour.
Quote them directly where it matters.
beginnerNote: to operate. The consent habit is the part people get wrong, and it is not optional.
pricingNote: Speakwise reported at approx. $59.99/year. Rechat AI Memo included at no additional cost for existing Rechat users. Plaud pricing not published on its real estate page (hardware plus subscription model). VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: HIGHEST CONSENT RISK IN THIS BATCH. US recording law splits: roughly 38 states plus DC allow one-party consent, while about 11 - including California, Florida, Illinois, Maryland and Washington - require all-party consent. Get verbal consent on the recording regardless of your state. Recordings of client conversations are business records that may be discoverable; check your brokerage's retention policy before you build a habit around this.

persona: Buyer's agent with a client who can't see past dated decor
title: I want to show my buyer what this dated house could look like after a renovation
intentLabels: see potential in a fixer upper
redesign a room from a photo
workflowSummary: Take a clear photo of the room during the showing, upload it, and generate a version with the change the buyer is imagining - new cabinets, different paint, floors, furniture. Good tools keep the walls, windows and dimensions intact and only change the finishes, which is the point: a render that quietly moves a wall creates an expectation no contractor can meet. Use it to unstick a buyer who cannot visualise, then immediately get a contractor to price the actual work before it influences what they offer.
samplePrompt:
Generate a renovation preview of this kitchen: replace the [oak] cabinets with [shaker, warm white], change the countertop to [quartz], and update the flooring to [wide-plank oak].
Keep the walls, windows, ceiling height, cabinet layout and room dimensions exactly as they are in the photo. Do not move or remove any structural element. Do not change the window views.
Generate three variations at different price points from a light refresh to a full replacement.
beginnerNote: upload a photo, describe the change.
pricingNote: Renovate AI states 1,000 free visualisation credits for business workflow integration; consumer pricing not published on the landing page. Comparable tools advertise free tiers with paid credit packs. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Renders are not plans and AI renovation cost estimates are not quotes. If an agent generates a render that influences a purchase decision, and the work turns out to be structurally impossible or costs three times the estimate, that is a real exposure - label every render clearly as a concept and route costing to a licensed contractor. Do not put speculative renders in MLS listing photos.

persona: Agent working with buyers who don't speak the local language fluently
title: I want to explain listings and documents to a buyer in their own language

tools.name: Claude, ChatGPT or DeepL (for informal communication and listing copy)
X-doc AI or Stepes (for documents needing certified translation)

workflowSummary: Split the work by stakes. For informal communication, listing summaries and neighbourhood explanations, a general AI assistant is fine and fast, but have a fluent human check the tone before it goes out - property idioms like 'move-in ready' and 'charming fixer-upper' translate badly and can imply something you did not mean. For anything binding - purchase agreements, disclosures, leases, deeds - use a certified translation service with human linguist review. Some jurisdictions require a certified translation for a contract to be enforceable.
samplePrompt:
Translate the following into [language] for a prospective buyer: [paste].
Rules:
- Use natural, everyday [language], not literal translation. Do not translate real estate idioms literally - rewrite them so the meaning survives.
- Keep all numbers, measurements, dates and addresses exactly as written, and add the local unit equivalent in brackets where measurement systems differ.
- Do not translate legal terms that have no equivalent - leave the original term and add a short plain-language explanation.
- At the end, list anything you were unsure about so I can have it checked.
beginnerNote: for informal communication. No for contracts - that is a certified-translation job, not an AI task.
pricingNote: General assistants: free tier or approx. $20/mo. Certified document translation is quoted per document and not published. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING - the vendor-published accuracy figures in this category (e.g. '99% accuracy across 100+ languages') are self-reported marketing claims.
accessNotes: Never rely on machine translation for a document a client signs. Some jurisdictions require certified translation for enforceability, and a mistranslated contingency is a liability that sits with the agent, not the tool. Also a fair-housing point: offering service in a buyer's language is good practice, but the quality of service must not differ by language.

persona: Home inspector serving buyer clients
title: I want to write up my inspection reports faster without making them harder for buyers to read

tools.name: a voice dictation tool for on-site notes

workflowSummary: Capture observations on site as photos plus short voice or text notes rather than typing narratives in the field. The AI turns those observations into buyer-readable comments matched to your existing approved template language, so the voice stays yours and stays consistent across reports. Review every generated comment before the report goes out - your name and licence are on it. The gain is largely in the executive summary and the repair-request-ready formatting, which is what actually reduces follow-up calls from agents and buyers.
samplePrompt:
Turn these on-site observations into report comments for a buyer audience:
[paste observations]
For each: state what was observed factually, why it matters, and the recommended action. Plain language, no jargon a buyer would need to look up. Neutral and professional tone - do not use alarming language and do not minimise.
Do not state a cause you cannot see, do not estimate repair costs, and do not describe anything I did not observe. If an item was inaccessible or not tested, say so explicitly.
beginnerNote: the AI features sit inside inspection software inspectors already use.
pricingNote: Not published on the vendor's homepage. Vendor states 12,000+ inspectors on the platform. Report Assist described as early access. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: The inspector's licence and liability attach to every generated comment - vendor states all AI output passes through the inspector's review, and it must. An AI narrative that implies a cause or condition the inspector did not observe is a professional liability issue, not a wording problem. Check whether your state licensing board has any position on AI-assisted report generation.

persona: Agent on the road between appointments
title: I want to capture tasks and property notes by voice while I'm driving between showings
workflowSummary: Speak the note as it occurs to you rather than trying to remember it until you are at a desk - the address, what happened, and what you need to do about it. The tool separates the task from the context, sets a reminder, and files the note against the right property or client. This is distinct from recording client conversations: you are dictating to yourself, so there is no consent question. Review the day's captures once each evening and push the real commitments into your CRM, because a voice note nobody reads is the same as no note.
samplePrompt:
Here are my raw voice notes from today: [paste transcript].
Separate them into:
1. Tasks with a deadline - who, what, by when.
2. Notes about a specific property or client, grouped by address or name.
3. Things I said I would send someone.
4. Anything ambiguous where I need to check what I meant.
Keep my wording where it carries meaning. Do not invent deadlines I did not state.
beginnerNote: press record and talk.
pricingNote: Vendor states free to get started; paid tiers and CRM integrations described as coming soon. Young product with limited independent review coverage. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Dictating to yourself avoids the recording-consent issue that applies to row 12, but the notes still contain client information and property details - check where the vendor stores them and whether your brokerage permits it. Do not dictate while driving; use a hands-free trigger or pull over.

persona: Buyer's agent or buyer reviewing the title commitment
title: I want to understand what the title commitment actually says before we close
intentLabels: what are these exceptions on my title

tools.name: TheLawGPT or a comparable legal AI (for a structured read)
your title company and a real estate attorney (for anything material)

workflowSummary: Title commitments are short, dense and almost never read by buyers, which is how people discover an easement across the driveway after closing. Get a structured summary of the Schedule B exceptions with each one explained in plain language, flag anything non-standard for the property type and jurisdiction, and cross-check the exceptions against the seller's disclosures and the survey for contradictions. Then take the flagged items to the title company or an attorney inside the objection period, which is usually short and unforgiving.
samplePrompt:
I've attached a title commitment for a residential purchase in [state].
1. List every Schedule B exception and explain in plain language what each one actually restricts or permits.
2. Flag which are standard boilerplate for a residential property in this jurisdiction and which are not.
3. Identify anything that could affect use of the property - easements, encroachments, restrictions, mineral rights, liens.
4. List what I should ask the title company about, ranked by importance.
Quote the commitment's own language for every item. Do not tell me whether the title is acceptable. This is not legal advice.
beginnerNote: the summary is easy to get, but knowing which exceptions matter in your jurisdiction is genuinely specialist and the objection window is short.
pricingNote: Not published on the vendor's page; a free first-document upload is advertised. General assistants: free tier or approx. $20/mo. Attorney title review is separately priced. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Not legal advice, and title is one of the areas where that caveat has teeth - a missed exception is generally not recoverable after closing. Title commitments contain the parties' names and the legal description; redact or use a private workspace. Agents summarising title exceptions for a client are close to unauthorised practice of law in several states - route the analysis to the title company or an attorney and keep your own role to making sure the buyer reads it.

persona: Principal broker or compliance officer at a small-to-mid brokerage
title: I want every transaction file checked for missing signatures and disclosures before it closes, not after an audit finds it
workflowSummary: Connect the tool to wherever your files already live - most plug into your existing transaction management or back office system rather than requiring a new one. It runs a state-aware first-pass review on every file as it moves through the pipeline, checking signatures, dates, required disclosures and state-specific forms, and surfaces exceptions on a dashboard with the specific document, page and party involved. The broker or compliance officer still makes every final call - the tool's job is making sure review time goes to genuine problems instead of paging through complete, compliant files one at a time.
samplePrompt: Not an AI prompt for this workflow - it is a configuration decision. Before rollout, confirm with the vendor: which states are covered (state-specific requirements vary and not every vendor covers every state), whether the tool integrates with your existing transaction management system or requires migrating files into a new one, and what happens to a flagged exception - does it block closing, notify the compliance officer, or just log it. Get this in writing before agents start relying on it to catch their mistakes.
beginnerNote: the tool runs itself once configured, but the setup decisions (state coverage, escalation rules, integration) need a compliance officer's judgement, not an agent's.
pricingNote: Not published on the ReBillion product page. Industry roundups cite compliance-focused tools generally reducing manual review time by 50-70% but do not cite a specific ReBillion price. SkySlope and BoldTrail BackOffice pricing is quote-based, scaled by agent count. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Explicitly a workflow aid, not legal advice, per the vendor's own language - the broker remains accountable for every closed file regardless of what the tool flagged or missed. Coverage is state-specific (one vendor's tool covers ten named US states as of this writing) - confirm your state is covered before relying on it, and have a fallback manual process for states it does not cover.

persona: Managing broker or office manager scanning agent-published content
title: I want to catch fair housing problems in agent listings and social posts before a complaint gets filed, not after

tools.name: The free Fair Housing checker at listingkit.app/tools

workflowSummary: Paste any piece of copy - MLS remarks, a social caption, an ad - into a checker built specifically for the eight federally protected classes, not a generic grammar tool. The check works on property-versus-occupant: it should catch 'perfect for families' as a real violation while leaving 'master bedroom' alone, since the second is permitted despite sounding similar. Make this step mandatory rather than optional in your brokerage's publishing workflow, because the step that gets skipped under deadline pressure is the one that mattered. Track flagged content over time - a pattern from one agent is a training conversation, not just a series of one-off saves.
samplePrompt:
Review this listing copy for Fair Housing Act compliance across all eight protected classes (race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, disability, plus any additional classes protected under [state] law):
[paste copy]
For each flagged phrase: quote it exactly, name which protected class it implicates, explain why it describes a preferred occupant rather than the property, and suggest a property-focused replacement.
Do not flag terms HUD has explicitly confirmed as permitted (e.g. 'master bedroom', 'walk to town'). Distinguish clearly between a real violation and an overcautious false flag.
beginnerNote: paste text, get an eight-class analysis, no account required for the free version.
pricingNote: Free standalone checker, no account required. ListingKit's integrated generation-plus-scanning platform pricing not published on the cited page. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
sourceType: Vendor blog page (product page for the checker itself not separately captured)
accessNotes: The agent who publishes the content is liable, not the software, and using a checker does not transfer that responsibility - this is true whether the copy was AI-drafted or human-written. A checker catching zero violations across a large sample may mean the checker is set too loose, not that everything published was clean - spot-audit against known bad examples periodically. NAR Code of Ethics obligations and HUD advertising guidance are separate from state and local MLS rules; a brokerage needs all three, not just the federal baseline.

persona: Broker-owner or franchise recruiting director
title: I want to know which agents in my market are actually worth recruiting, and which of my own agents might leave
workflowSummary: Connect the tool to your MLS data rather than trying to build recruiting lists from memory or word of mouth - it converts raw production, listing and closing records into a ranked view of who is actually performing in your market, including agents at competing firms. Use the predictive retention scoring to see which of your own agents show early signs of flight risk based on production and behaviour patterns, and get ahead of the conversation rather than being surprised by a resignation. Treat the output as a lead list and a coaching signal, not gospel - it is a data model, and the relationship conversation with an agent still has to happen face to face.
samplePrompt: Not an AI prompt for this workflow - it is a data platform, not a conversational tool. Before subscribing, ask the vendor directly: which MLSs does this cover in my market (coverage is MLS-dependent, and gaps mean blind spots), how is the 'switch risk' score calculated and what is its published accuracy, and can I export the underlying data if I cancel. Get a trial period and check the output against three agents whose situations you already know well before trusting it on people you don't.
beginnerNote: the entry-level tier is built to be simple, but acting well on the output (a recruiting conversation, a retention conversation) is a leadership skill, not a software feature.
pricingNote: Entry-level 'XPress' tier reported at a flat $69.95/month in select US markets. The full platform is reported starting around $350/month plus MLS fees, scaling with agent count and modules. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING - the two tiers differ substantially and both figures appear in vendor material.
accessNotes: Predictive 'switch risk' and production scores are modelled estimates, not certainties, and a false positive - approaching an agent who was not actually leaving, or missing one who was - has real relationship cost. This is licensed MLS data used for competitive intelligence on agents at other firms; confirm your MLS's data-use terms permit this before relying on it for recruiting outreach.

persona: Team lead or brokerage owner building a new-agent onboarding program
title: I want new agents productive in their first 90 days without me personally training each one

tools.name: the Agent Management Portal (Icenhower Coaching & Training)
a general AI assistant to draft the initial curriculum from your own materials

workflowSummary: Build the 90-day plan around a single goal - getting the agent to their first deal without an avoidable mistake - rather than trying to cover everything at once. Load your brokerage's own materials (contracts, forms, local market stats, branding guidelines) into the platform so onboarding is specific to your office, not generic content licensed from elsewhere. Use the accountability dashboard so you can see who is actually moving through the material and who has stalled, and set up in-app leaderboards or recognition if that fits your team's culture - gamification measurably helps some teams and does nothing for others, so watch your own group rather than assuming.
samplePrompt:
I'm building a 90-day onboarding program for new buyer's agents at my brokerage in [area]. Structure it into weekly modules covering: database and CRM setup, lead generation habits, our specific contracts and forms, local market fundamentals, showing and negotiation basics, and compliance essentials.
For each week, give me: the single most important outcome, two or three concrete tasks (not just reading), and one thing I should check with the agent directly rather than assume they've absorbed.
Keep it realistic for someone doing this alongside real client work, not a full-time course load.
beginnerNote: to draft the structure. The follow-through - actually checking in with each agent - remains a person's job, not the software's.
pricingNote: Not published on the Agently product page. Icenhower's Agent Management Portal pricing not published - offered as part of broader coaching engagements. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Vendor-reported retention improvements from gamification and structured onboarding are self-reported and not independently audited - treat as directional, not a guarantee for your specific team. If agents are independent contractors rather than employees in your jurisdiction, mandatory training structures can have employment-classification implications; check with your broker's counsel before making any onboarding module compulsory in a way that resembles employee supervision.

persona: Team leader responsible for coaching a roster too large to coach personally
title: I want every agent on my team to get real 1:1 coaching on their sales calls, not just a group pep talk

tools.name: a human sales manager for the agents flagged as needing the most attention

workflowSummary: Connect the tool to your CRM and dialer, which takes about five minutes, and calls begin getting graded automatically as they happen. Every agent gets a weekly coaching session built from their own call history rather than a generic script - for a team of any size, this is coaching depth a single human manager cannot deliver past roughly ten to fifteen people. Use the team-wide report to see patterns across the whole roster and target your own limited time on the agents the data says need it most, rather than splitting your attention evenly regardless of who needs help.
samplePrompt: Not a single AI prompt for this workflow - the coaching sessions are voice-to-voice and generated automatically from call data once configured. Before rollout, confirm with your team: what gets recorded and where it is stored, whether agents can review their own scored calls before a coaching session happens automatically, and how disagreements about a low score get resolved. Treat the weekly report as a coaching-priority list for you, not a performance review document, until your team has used it long enough to trust the scoring.
beginnerNote: to set up - a five-minute CRM connection. The judgement is in how you use the aggregate report as a leader.
pricingNote: Solo agent tier reported at $49/month, billed quarterly with a 7-day free trial. Team/brokerage pricing reported starting around $5.80 per call hour for teams of 50+ agents, with custom pricing above that. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Recording sales calls is subject to the same one-party versus all-party consent rules that apply to any recorded call - confirm your state's requirement and your existing client-communication consent language covers this use before turning it on team-wide. The vendor's own case-study statistics (churn rates, lead-cost figures) are self-reported industry context, not measured outcomes of this specific product - do not present them to your team as a guaranteed result.

persona: Broker-owner or CFO managing agent commission payouts
title: I want commission splits, caps and team overrides calculated automatically instead of by hand every closing

tools.name: BoldTrail BackOffice (formerly Brokermint) for simpler structures

workflowSummary: Map your actual commission structures first - traditional splits, graduated caps that reset annually, team leader overrides, mentor splits on new agent transactions, franchise royalties, referral waterfalls - because the platform you need depends entirely on how complex that list is. Simple flat splits work on nearly any tool including a spreadsheet; once caps, overrides and multi-party splits stack up, you need a dedicated platform. Once configured, a closing should trigger the disbursement calculation, the compliance checklist, and the agent's pay stub automatically, with every calculation logged and timestamped for audit purposes.
samplePrompt: Not an AI prompt for this workflow - it is a back-office configuration task, not something to ask a chatbot to do with real commission data. Before choosing a platform, list out every commission structure your brokerage actually runs, including edge cases (a referral fee waterfall, a mentor split that only applies to a new agent's first three deals), and confirm in writing with each vendor that their platform handles every one of them, not just the common cases the demo shows.
beginnerNote: this is a back-office system implementation, not a beginner task. Get your accountant or a transaction coordinator involved in setup.
pricingNote: Loft47 pricing is based on agent count; higher tiers add AI-driven document ingestion and automated compliance review, plus an additional $47 per deal for full-service deal creation. Comparable platforms (SkySlope Commissions, Ngage Plus) reported at $500-$1,500+/month for full-depth automation; enterprise platforms (Lone Wolf BrokerWolf) are custom-quoted. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING - published figures vary by more than 3x depending on vendor and tier.
accessNotes: A commission calculation error compounds across every transaction it touches and is a real financial and 1099 liability, not a cosmetic bug - independently audit the platform's output against manual calculations for at least the first month on every commission structure type you run, not just a sample. Trust accounting rules vary by state (one vendor cites compliance with 39 US states and 6 Canadian provinces) - confirm your state is covered.

persona: Team leader or ops manager fielding leads from multiple portals
title: I want new leads assigned to the right agent automatically instead of a manager reviewing and assigning them by hand

tools.name: Sisu (for teams already using it for production tracking)

workflowSummary: Start simple - pure round-robin works fine for a small team where everyone covers the same footprint and handles similar leads - and only add complexity (zip code, price tier, language, luxury specialisation) once round-robin visibly starts sending the wrong lead to the wrong agent. Configure a fallback rule for anything that does not match your primary routing logic, so an unmapped zip code or an unusual price point does not sit unassigned. Give team leaders a dashboard view of which leads are going unworked and which agents are engaging quickly, so slow response times surface before the lead goes cold rather than after.
samplePrompt: Not a single AI prompt for this workflow - it is CRM routing-rule configuration. Before building your rules, answer: does round-robin fail today because agents have genuinely different specialties (luxury, first-time buyer, bilingual), or does it just feel unfair? Only add routing complexity for the first reason. Write down your fallback rule for anything that doesn't match a primary rule before you launch, not after the first lead falls through the gap.
beginnerNote: to configure basic round-robin. Somewhat once you add multiple routing dimensions - that setup benefits from a person who understands both the CRM and how the team actually specialises.
pricingNote: Follow Up Boss reported starting around $69/month for solo agents, scaling past $1,000/month for large teams; specific team-tier and routing-feature pricing not published on a single page. BoldTrail and Sisu pricing are quote-based. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
