accessNotes: Routing a lead to the 'right' agent by price tier or specialty can shade into discriminatory steering if the routing criteria correlate with a protected class rather than genuine agent expertise - keep routing rules documented and defensible on business grounds (language spoken, price-band experience, geographic license) rather than proxies for who a buyer or seller is. TCPA consent requirements for the routed agent's first contact travel with the lead, not just with the brokerage.

persona: Team leader or brokerage owner reviewing team performance
title: I want to ask plain questions about my team's numbers instead of digging through reports myself
workflowSummary: For teams already tracking transactions, activity and profitability in a platform, use the AI layer to ask direct questions in plain English - where contracts are stalling, which agents' activity has quietly gone dark, what changing a split or adding an ISA would do to net income - rather than building a new report every time a question comes up. For smaller teams without that infrastructure, export whatever production data you do have (a spreadsheet is fine) and ask a general assistant the same kind of question. Either way, use the answer to start a coaching conversation, not to replace one - the tool surfaces the pattern, the leader still has to talk to the agent.
samplePrompt:
Here is my team's production data for the last quarter: [paste - agent name, leads, appointments, contracts, closings, GCI].
Answer these as if you were coaching me:
1. Which agents are trending down, and does the drop show up earlier in the funnel (fewer appointments) or later (contracts falling through)?
2. Where does the team seem to be losing the most potential GCI - lead volume, conversion, or deal size?
3. If I could have one coaching conversation this week, who should it be with and what would I ask them?
Base this only on the numbers I've given you - do not assume causes I haven't described.
beginnerNote: for the general-assistant version with an exported report. Somewhat for the full Sisu/Sunburst version - the value depends on having clean data already flowing into the platform.
pricingNote: Sisu base plans reported at $333-$999/month depending on billing term, plus $17-$21 per user - Sunburst AI coaching bundled into higher tiers. Third-party estimates for a 10-agent team using Sisu alongside a separate CRM run to roughly $1,100-$1,250/month all-in. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING - figures vary noticeably by source.
accessNotes: AI-suggested causes for a production drop (e.g. 'lead source X is underperforming') are pattern-matches on the data given, not verified diagnoses - confirm with the agent before acting on an inference, since a real explanation (a family emergency, a market-specific issue) may not be visible in the numbers at all. Surfacing an individual agent's activity data to a leader has real workplace-relations weight; be deliberate about who sees granular per-agent reports.

persona: Brokerage marketing lead building recruiting outreach
title: I want to send recruiting emails to prospective agents that don't read as mass-blasted spam

tools.name: a general AI assistant for one-off personalised notes

workflowSummary: Pull the prospective agent's actual recent activity - a specific closing, a listing that just went pending, a niche they clearly specialise in - rather than sending a templated 'have you considered a change' email to a purchased list. Purpose-built tools do this by connecting production data directly to the email draft, so the personalisation is grounded in something real rather than looking personalised while saying nothing specific. Keep the list small enough that every send gets a human read before it goes out; a recruiting email that gets a fact wrong about the recipient's own business does more damage than a generic one would have.
samplePrompt:
I'm reaching out to a real estate agent I'd like to recruit. Here's what I know about their recent business: [paste - recent closings, specialty, market area, any public info].
Draft a short, specific recruiting email that references one real thing about their business, states clearly why I'm reaching out, and makes one concrete ask (a fifteen-minute call). No generic flattery, no vague promises about 'culture' or 'support' without specifics. Under 120 words.
Do not invent any detail about their business I haven't given you.
beginnerNote: the personalisation is only as good as the data feeding it, and purpose-built recruiting-data tools do this more reliably than a general assistant working from whatever you happen to know.
pricingNote: Relitix MessageAI pricing not published standalone - bundled into the broader Relitix platform (see Relitix batch pricing note). Brokerkit offers multiple pricing tiers scaled by brokerage size, not published in detail. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Recruiting emails are still subject to CAN-SPAM (working unsubscribe, physical address, no deceptive subject lines) even though the recipient is a fellow licensee rather than a consumer. Using licensed MLS production data to identify and target a specific agent at a competing firm should be checked against your MLS's data-use terms before building an outreach campaign around it.

persona: Team leader managing agents across bilingual or multi-market territories
title: I want to route a Spanish-speaking lead to a Spanish-speaking agent automatically instead of hoping whoever answers can help

tools.name: Follow Up Boss or BoldTrail (custom routing rule using an agent attribute field)

workflowSummary: Add a language attribute to each agent's profile in your CRM or routing system, then build a routing rule that checks the lead's stated or detected language preference against that attribute before falling back to round-robin. For inbound calls where language is not stated up front, a multilingual AI phone system can detect it early in the call and route accordingly rather than connecting the caller to someone who cannot help and creating a bad first impression. Keep a real fallback path for languages none of your agents speak - route to a general intake queue with a translation tool rather than dropping the lead.
samplePrompt: Not a single AI prompt for this workflow - it is a CRM attribute and routing-rule setup task. Before building it, confirm: which languages does my team actually cover, at what fluency (conversational is not the same as being able to walk someone through a purchase agreement), and what happens to a lead in a language nobody on the team speaks well. Write that fallback path down explicitly rather than leaving it implicit.
beginnerNote: to configure the routing rule itself. The harder part is accurately assessing each agent's actual working fluency, not just whether they speak the language socially.
pricingNote: No incremental cost beyond the CRM's existing routing feature in most platforms - this is a configuration, not a separate product. Multilingual AI phone systems (RingCentral AIR and similar) are priced separately and not captured here. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Overstating an agent's language fluency to a client and then having them struggle through a purchase agreement in that language is a real client-service failure, not just an inconvenience - verify fluency level honestly, not aspirationally, when building the attribute. This pairs with the buyer-side translation and interpretation workflow covered in the buyer-side batch; the routing decision here and the in-conversation support there are two different steps in the same client journey.

persona: Brokerage operations manager preparing for a state regulatory audit
title: I want to know before the state does whether our files would pass a compliance audit

tools.name: AI Compliance for Realtors checklist tools (aiandrealtors.com)
your compliance-focused transaction management platform's existing reporting

workflowSummary: Run a compliance-report pass across every open and recently closed file well before an audit is scheduled, not in the scramble after a notice arrives - the report should show which transactions have complete documentation and which have gaps requiring attention, tied to a recognised framework like ALTA Best Practices for the financial side. Use the gap list to close out missing items on active files immediately, and treat repeated gaps from the same source (a specific agent, a specific form) as a training issue rather than a one-off fix. Keep the audit-readiness report itself as a dated record showing you were proactively monitoring compliance, which matters if a regulator later asks about your office's general practices.
samplePrompt: Not an AI prompt for this workflow - it is a periodic compliance-reporting process, best run on a recurring schedule (e.g. monthly) rather than reactively. When reviewing the gap report, ask for each flagged file: is this missing, or just filed somewhere the tool didn't check? Confirm before treating a flag as a real compliance gap, since integration gaps between systems can produce false positives that look identical to genuine missing documents.
beginnerNote: running the report is simple once configured, but interpreting which gaps are urgent and which are false positives from a system integration issue takes someone who knows the file.
pricingNote: Not published for any of the cited tools in this specific audit-readiness configuration. Industry sources cite AI-powered compliance monitoring reducing manual review time by 50-70% broadly, without a specific tool or price attached to that figure. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: An AI compliance tool is a first-pass filter, explicitly not a substitute for the broker's own review or for legal counsel ahead of a known audit - if you have an actual audit notice in hand, involve your brokerage's attorney, not just software. The 50-70% efficiency figure cited industry-wide is a general claim, not a measured result for any specific tool - do not present it to a broker as an expected outcome.

persona: Broker-owner deciding whether to build an all-in-one AI-native back office or keep separate point tools
title: I want to know if switching to one AI-native platform is worth it or if I should keep the separate tools I already have
workflowSummary: Map your current stack first - which tool handles compliance, which handles transaction coordination, which handles commissions - and total the actual monthly cost and the hours your team spends moving data between them manually. An all-in-one platform's pitch is that it reads every file the moment it arrives from any source (email, e-signature, shared drive) and runs compliance and coordination across the whole file flow automatically, rather than requiring someone to feed documents into separate single-purpose tools one at a time. That consolidation has a real cost too - migrating existing files and retraining staff on one system - so weigh it against your current pain, not against the vendor's ideal-case description of the problem.
samplePrompt: Not an AI prompt for this workflow - it is a vendor evaluation and procurement decision. Before committing, ask any all-in-one vendor for: a list of current customers of similar brokerage size you can actually call, the real migration timeline and cost for your current file volume, and what specifically happens to files already in progress during a mid-quarter switch. Get these answers in writing, not in a sales call.
beginnerNote: this is a strategic buying decision for a broker-owner, not something to delegate to an AI tool or hand to a junior team member.
pricingNote: Not published for Joymore. Industry comparison pieces describe it as a newer entrant competing against established point solutions (ListedKit AI, DocJacket, MaxHome AI, BrokerBot) without publishing its own pricing. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING - this is one of the least price-transparent categories in the whole niche.
accessNotes: This source is a vendor's own comparison of itself against competitors - treat the specific claims of superiority with real skepticism and verify independently rather than citing this page's framing to a broker as neutral market research. A consolidation decision made on outdated competitive information (e.g. still referencing 'kvCORE' or 'BrokerMint' as separate brands after the 2024 BoldTrail rebrand) signals a source that has not been updated recently - check publish dates carefully in this category.

persona: Brokerage trainer or operations lead building internal AI-use training
title: I want to teach my agents how to use AI properly instead of just telling them tools exist

tools.name: Claude or ChatGPT as the live-build tool during the session itself
your brokerage's own listing/compliance materials as the training data

workflowSummary: Structure the session around one live build using an agent's own real listing rather than a tour of five different tools, because watching a demo produces admiration and building something produces adoption. Teach the underlying skill of describing what you want clearly and iterating on the output - prompt structure - rather than a list of exact prompts to memorise, since a fixed prompt list goes stale the moment the underlying model changes. Build the Fair Housing and advertising-rule guardrails into the session itself, using your brokerage's actual compliance requirements, not a generic list, and end with a clear handoff into whatever CRM or transaction system agents actually use day to day.
samplePrompt:
I'm running a one-hour AI training session for [number] agents at my brokerage. Help me structure it around a single live build: taking one agent's real, current listing and using AI to draft the MLS description, a social caption, and a check for Fair Housing issues, all in front of the group.
Give me: a rough timeline for the hour, three or four discussion prompts to ask the group as we build (not just watch), and a short list of Fair Housing and advertising-rule points to fold into the live build rather than teach as a separate lecture.
Assume the agents have varying comfort levels with AI tools, from skeptical to already using them daily.
beginnerNote: to plan the session using a general assistant. The delivery itself is a facilitation skill, not a tool-operation skill.
pricingNote: Free to plan using any AI assistant's free tier or approx. $20/mo paid tier. External coaching companies charge separately for delivered training programs, not published here. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: The source cites NAR's 2026 Member Profile figures on agent income and expenses (median gross income $59,200, median expenses $9,530) as context for training urgency - these are industry-wide medians and should not be presented to an individual agent as a guaranteed benchmark. Fair Housing and advertising-rule content used in training must reflect your specific state and MLS rules, not just federal HUD guidance - a generic training session that only covers federal law leaves state-specific gaps.

persona: Broker-owner comparing back-office platforms to switch to or add
title: I want a straight comparison of the major brokerage back-office platforms before I sign a contract
intentLabels: Loft47 vs Lone Wolf vs BoldTrail

tools.name: A general AI assistant to synthesise vendor comparison pages you provide
plus direct vendor demos - do not rely on any single comparison page as neutral

workflowSummary: Gather comparison content from multiple sources, including at least one page published by each vendor being compared (since a vendor's comparison of itself against competitors is marketing, not neutral analysis) and at least one independent trade publication or review site. Feed the set to an AI assistant and ask it to build a single side-by-side table on the dimensions that actually matter for your brokerage - commission complexity supported, compliance workflow depth, integration breadth, and total cost of ownership at your actual agent count - rather than accepting any one source's framing of which platform 'wins'. Then book demos with your top two and test them against your own messiest real commission structure, not the demo's clean example.
samplePrompt:
I'm comparing back-office platforms for a [size]-agent brokerage. I've attached comparison content from several sources: [paste or attach].
Build a single side-by-side table covering: commission plan complexity supported, compliance and audit-trail features, integrations with [my current CRM/transaction system], and published or estimated pricing at my agent count.
Flag clearly which claims come from a vendor's own page about itself, which come from a vendor's page about a competitor, and which come from an independent source - keep these three categories visibly separate rather than blending them into one voice.
Do not declare a winner - give me the comparison so I can decide.
beginnerNote: this is exactly the kind of synthesis-from-multiple-documents task a general AI assistant handles well, as long as you feed it a genuinely mixed set of sources.
pricingNote: Free with any AI assistant's free tier or approx. $20/mo paid tier for the synthesis step itself; the platforms being compared carry the pricing detailed in row 6 of this batch. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Vendor-published comparison pages (including several cited across this batch) have a structural incentive to favour themselves - explicitly telling the AI assistant to separate vendor self-comparisons from independent sources, as the prompt does, meaningfully improves the reliability of the synthesis.

persona: Team leader running a weekly or monthly team meeting
title: I want to turn our team meeting into a written summary and action list automatically instead of someone taking notes
intentLabels: automated meeting minutes for real estate teams
workflowSummary: Let the tool capture the meeting audio, whether in person or on a video call, and generate a structured summary afterward rather than assigning someone to take notes during the meeting, which pulls their attention away from actually participating. Review the generated action items immediately after the meeting while the context is fresh, correcting anything the tool mis-assigned before it goes out to the team. Distribute the summary the same day - a meeting recap sent a week later has lost most of its value because the momentum from the discussion has already faded.
samplePrompt:
Here is the transcript from today's team meeting: [paste].
Produce:
1. A short summary of what was actually decided, separate from what was merely discussed.
2. Every action item, with who owns it and by when, based only on what was explicitly said.
3. Anything that was raised but not resolved, so it can go on next week's agenda.
Keep it to one page. Do not infer a decision from a discussion that didn't reach a clear conclusion - list it as unresolved instead.
beginnerNote: the same tool most agents already use for showing notes works identically here.
pricingNote: Otter.ai has a functional free tier; Granola and Plaud pricing not repeated here (see the buyer-side batch entry for the same tools). VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Get verbal consent to record before the meeting starts, particularly in an all-party-consent state, even though this is an internal team meeting rather than a client call - the same consent principle applies regardless of who is in the room. Meeting recordings and transcripts are discoverable business records in some circumstances; check your brokerage's document retention policy before this becomes a standing habit.

persona: Brokerage marketing or brand compliance lead reviewing agent-generated content at scale
title: I want to check dozens of agent-created social posts and listing descriptions for brand and compliance issues without reading every single one myself

tools.name: a general AI assistant for smaller batches without a dedicated platform

workflowSummary: For a small brokerage, batch the week's agent-submitted content into one document and run it through a compliance and brand-tone check in a single pass rather than reviewing each post individually as it comes in. For a larger brokerage, a dedicated platform can score every AI-assisted interaction against your approved messaging and flag claims policy require review before anything goes public, giving your compliance team a dashboard view of what's being intercepted and why rather than reading every submission. Either way, the point is triage, not full automation - genuinely flagged content still needs a human compliance reviewer before it publishes.
samplePrompt:
Here are this week's agent-submitted social posts and listing blurbs: [paste batch, labelled by agent].
For each one, flag: any Fair Housing language issue, any claim that isn't clearly supported by facts I'd need to verify (investment promises, school ratings, safety claims), and any tone or messaging inconsistency with our brand voice guidelines [paste guidelines].
Group the output by severity - must-fix before publishing versus optional style suggestion - so I can prioritise my review time. Do not approve anything yourself; flag for my review only.
beginnerNote: for the batch-review-with-a-general-assistant approach at small scale. Somewhat for the dedicated platform - initial setup of your approved messaging library takes real time investment.
pricingNote: Socialsales.io pricing not published on the cited page. ListingKit pricing not published. General assistant batch review: free tier or approx. $20/mo. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: This is a scaled-up version of the individual-listing Fair Housing check in row 2 of this batch - the same 'agent who publishes is liable, not the software' principle applies at any volume. A dashboard that reports content trust scores and claims-intercepted counts is useful for spotting patterns, but a high score should not be read as a compliance guarantee; spot-check the platform's judgement against known difficult examples periodically.

persona: CRE acquisitions analyst or asset manager handling a multi-tenant property
title: I want the key terms out of a 90-page commercial lease without reading the whole thing myself

tools.name: Claude or ChatGPT for a handful of leases without a dedicated platform

workflowSummary: For a handful of leases, upload the document to a general AI assistant with a large context window and ask for a structured abstract against your own template - dates, rent schedule, escalations, renewal options, CAM provisions, termination rights. For a real portfolio (dozens to hundreds of leases), use a purpose-built platform that returns confidence scores on each extracted field, so you know which terms to trust and which to manually verify. Either way, an analyst still checks every abstracted term against the source clause before it enters a model - the tool removes the typing, not the judgement.
samplePrompt:
I've attached a commercial lease. Extract the following into a structured table: tenant name, lease start and end date, base rent and any escalation schedule, renewal options and notice periods, CAM/operating expense recovery method, security deposit, termination rights, co-tenancy clauses, and any assignment or subletting restrictions.
For each field, quote the exact source clause and page number it came from. If a field is genuinely absent from the document, say so rather than leaving it blank without explanation. Flag anything unusual or non-standard for a lease of this type.
beginnerNote: for a general assistant on a handful of leases. Somewhat for a dedicated platform at portfolio scale - setup and template mapping take real time.
pricingNote: Purpose-built tools reported at $15-$400+ per lease depending on tool and field depth (one platform: $15-$20 for a full extraction with a free preview). Enterprise document-intelligence platforms (e.g. Kira) reported starting around $2,500/month. General assistants: free tier or approx. $20/mo. For a 100-lease portfolio, total abstraction cost is reported to range from roughly $1,500 (AI software) to $40,000+ (traditional outsourced abstraction). VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Reported accuracy for leading platforms runs 90-97% on standard terms - the remaining error concentrates in non-standard clauses, complex escalation formulas, and cross-referenced exhibits, which is exactly where the financial stakes are highest. Every extracted term should be traceable back to its source clause; if a platform's output cannot be verified against the original lease, the time saved is not worth the underwriting risk it introduces.

persona: Acquisitions analyst screening inbound deals
title: I want to screen dozens of deals against my investment criteria without opening every offering memorandum myself

tools.name: a general AI assistant with your own criteria checklist for lower volume

workflowSummary: Define your actual investment criteria in writing first - asset class, geography, price range, cap rate floor, vintage, occupancy - because a screening tool is only as good as the thesis you give it. Feed each incoming OM or deal package to the tool and get back a scorecard against your criteria rather than opening every deal cold. Route only the deals that clear your bar to a full underwrite; use the tool to eliminate obvious non-fits, not to make the final go/no-go call, which still needs a person who knows the market.
samplePrompt:
Here is my firm's investment thesis: [paste - asset class, geography, price range, target cap rate, minimum occupancy, deal-breakers].
I've attached an offering memorandum. Score this deal against my thesis: which criteria does it clearly meet, which does it clearly fail, and which are ambiguous or need more information?
Do not recommend whether to pursue it - just tell me where it stands against what I've defined, and quote the OM for every claim.
beginnerNote: screening logic is simple to set up, but the value depends entirely on how precisely you've defined your own criteria before you start.
pricingNote: Apers AI reported at a flat $29.90/month for unlimited use - a notably low price point relative to the category that the source itself flags as worth scrutinising. Archer is custom-quoted, scaling by usage or a fixed unlimited tier. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: A screening tool that clears a deal is not an underwrite - it is a filter to decide what deserves a full underwrite. Multifamily-specific tools (Archer) do not extend to other asset classes; confirm asset-class fit before subscribing. An unusually low price for a stated feature set (as flagged for Apers AI above) warrants extra diligence on data handling and company stability before committing real deal flow to it.

persona: Acquisitions analyst building a first-pass underwriting model
title: I want a first-pass underwriting model built from the OM, rent roll and T-12 instead of building it from scratch every time

tools.name: a general AI assistant plus your own Excel template for other asset classes

workflowSummary: Upload the OM, rent roll and T-12 (trailing twelve months of operating statements) to the tool and let it populate your underwriting template - NOI, cap rate, DSCR at your target leverage, and a base/upside/downside IRR range. Purpose-built multifamily tools draw on their own market comps database for rent and sales comps; for other asset classes, a general assistant reading the documents directly and populating your own Excel template is the more flexible option. An experienced analyst still audits every formula and assumption before the model goes to IC - published accuracy for standard document extraction is high, but complex deal structures (multi-tier waterfalls, mixed-use capital stacks) still need human review.
samplePrompt:
I've attached an offering memorandum, a rent roll, and a T-12 operating statement for [property].
Populate my underwriting template with: in-place NOI, stabilized NOI assumptions and how you derived them, implied cap rate at the asking price, and a base/upside/downside case for year-one and year-five cash flow.
Quote the source document for every input. Flag any number that required an assumption on your part rather than coming directly from the documents, and explain the assumption.
Do not tell me whether to pursue the deal - just build the model inputs.
beginnerNote: document extraction into a template is straightforward; validating the resulting model against your firm's own underwriting standards takes real analyst judgement.
pricingNote: Archer: custom-quoted annual subscription, scaling by usage or a fixed unlimited tier. Blooma: enterprise/lender pricing, not published. General assistant: free tier or approx. $20/mo. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: Document extraction accuracy above 95% is reported for standard document types (OMs, rent rolls, T-12s) with proper citation and human review flags - complex deal structures (LIHTC, multi-tier waterfalls) carry materially more risk and need more scrutiny. A misplaced decimal in a rent roll extraction changes an acquisition decision; this is explicitly a high-stakes, low-error-tolerance workflow, not a casual drafting task.

persona: Commercial mortgage broker matching a deal to a lender
title: I want to know which lenders would actually consider this deal instead of cold-calling my contact list
workflowSummary: Upload the offering memorandum or enter deal details directly, and the tool matches the deal against current lender criteria across a large database of active loan programs, reading each lender's credit box in real time rather than relying on a static spreadsheet of who used to lend on what. Use the ranked list of matches as your outreach starting point - broker relationships and knowing which loan officer is actually looking at deals like this one still matter, but the tool removes the guesswork of which lenders to even approach.
samplePrompt: Not a single AI prompt for this workflow - deal details are entered or an OM uploaded directly into the platform, which returns matches automatically. Before relying on a ranked match list, confirm with the platform: how current is the underlying lender criteria data, and does a high match ranking reflect the lender's genuine current appetite or just a broad historical fit? A stale credit box is worse than no match at all if it sends you chasing a lender who quietly tightened criteria last month.
beginnerNote: upload the deal, get a ranked list. The relationship and negotiation work afterward is still the broker's job.
pricingNote: Not published on the cited announcement. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.
accessNotes: A ranked lender match is a starting point for outreach, not a commitment from any lender - treat it exactly like a prospecting list, not a term sheet. The vendor's own claimed database size (600,000+ loan programs, 1,000+ lenders) is a company-published figure and has not been independently verified in the source used here.

persona: CRE investor or acquisitions team preparing a deal for the investment committee
title: I want the investment committee memo built from the deal file instead of writing it from scratch for every deal

tools.name: a custom-built pipeline for firms with real deal volume and a fixed template
Claude or ChatGPT for lower-volume or one-off memos

workflowSummary: For occasional use, feed the OM, T-12, rent roll and your underwriting output to a general AI assistant along with your firm's own IC memo template, and get a full first draft - deal snapshot, thesis, risks and red flags, return math, recommendation - to edit rather than write from scratch. For firms doing enough volume that this repeats constantly, a packaged platform or a custom pipeline trained on your own template and voice pays for itself faster; the tradeoff is that a packaged tool tends to produce a generic-sounding memo unless it's been trained specifically on your firm's format.
samplePrompt:
I've attached the offering memorandum, T-12, rent roll, and my underwriting summary for [property], along with our firm's IC memo template.
Draft a complete IC memo following our template structure exactly: deal snapshot, investment thesis, market overview, risks and red flags, return projections, and recommendation.
Base every factual claim on the attached documents - quote the source for financial figures. Where the template calls for a judgement call (e.g. 'why this deal, why now'), draft your best attempt but flag it clearly as a draft opinion for the team to revise, not a fact.
beginnerNote: for the general-assistant version on occasional deals. Somewhat for a packaged or custom platform - real setup investment is required to make the output sound like your firm rather than generic.
pricingNote: Henry.ai pricing not published on the cited page (broader deal-workflow platform including OM and BOV generation). Custom-built pipelines are bespoke engagements, not published pricing. General assistant: free tier or approx. $20/mo. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING.

persona: Asset manager overseeing a multi-tenant office or retail portfolio
title: I want to know which leases are coming up for renewal and which tenants are actually at risk of leaving, across my whole portfolio

tools.name: VTS (lease roll and renewal risk monitoring)

workflowSummary: Centralize lease expiration dates, renewal options and notice periods across the whole portfolio in one place rather than tracking them property by property in separate spreadsheets, since the real risk in a multi-property portfolio is a renewal deadline that gets missed because no single person owned tracking it. Use predictive demand signals and market benchmarking to flag which upcoming expirations carry real renewal risk (below-market current rent, a tenant showing reduced space utilization) versus routine renewals unlikely to churn. Get ahead of at-risk renewals with a retention conversation months before the notice deadline, not after a tenant has already signed elsewhere.

Here is our portfolio's lease expiration schedule for the next 12 months: [paste - property, tenant, expiration date, current rent, notice period, any known tenant issues].
Help me prioritise: which expirations carry the highest combined risk (large tenant, below-market rent gap suggesting they could get a better deal elsewhere, or any noted issues) and should get a retention conversation started now versus which look routine.
Do not assume a tenant will renew or vacate - just help me rank where my limited attention should go first, based only on what I've given you.
beginnerNote: the platform view is straightforward once populated, but populating it accurately across a real portfolio, and having the retention conversations themselves, takes real asset-management work.

persona: CRE firm principal deciding how much to invest in an AI tool stack versus a single all-in-one platform

A custom-built pipeline trained on your firm's own template and voice costs more and takes longer to stand up but fits precisely once built.
